votes.reasoning: PinStore.swift: set and clear now use do/catch with AppLog.pinning.error and return false on failure. The in-memory memo is still updated first, as before. In clear, CocoaError.fileNoSuchFile counts as success, so clearing a host that was never pinned is not reported as a failure, and a test covers that. Reversal check: forcing true on the failure paths made the tests at PinStoreTests.swift:39 and :70 fail.

PinStore.swift:56-91. The two `try?` calls became do/catch with AppLog.pinning.error and a @discardableResult Bool, so the PinningDelegate.swift:67/91 call sites are unchanged. Treating CocoaError.fileNoSuchFile as success in clear() is the right semantics, and the doc comment says so. The write keeps AtomicFileWrite.write(..., permissions: 0o600), which satisfies the hard rule on secret files. The added doc comments explain intent rather than repeating the code.

PinStore.set and clear now return @discardableResult Bool. Callers are PinningDelegate.swift:67 and :91 plus main.swift:1290-1304, and all compile as they are. Pins are still written with AtomicFileWrite at 0o600, so the secret-permission rule still holds. clear treats a missing pin file (fileNoSuchFile) as success. It logs to AppLog.pinning, which already exists. Pin format and path are unchanged.
